correctness.rationale: This is the farthest orthogonal projection on complete lines with fixed ties, not a return map restricted in advance to the boundary. In an acute triangle a vertex goes to the interior of the opposite edge, and edge interiors never map to vertices. Thus vertex cycles are excluded. Every three-word with distinct successive line labels visits all three lines; a four-word either alternates two lines (its unique affine fixed point is their intersection) or has a single repeated line. Each designated affine return is a strict contraction on the complete starting line. For a normalized repeated side AB with C=(u,w), the return candidate computed in RESULT.md §2 is unique. Comparing distances at the four candidate points gives bD>u^2(a+b), (1-u)(1+b)>D, b(a+b)>D and u(1+a)>D. At u=1/2 the two leg-point tests coincide and are equivalent to 4s^2-2s-1<0 for s=sqrt(v^2+1/4); for a repeated leg one necessary test instead gives (s^2-1/2)^2<0. Thus the unique four-cycle ends exactly at v=sqrt(phi)/2 where the two ties are fixed. For a three-word use m=1/(1+2s^2); the three perpendicular-distance tests are m<1/2, m<1/(1+s), and 2m>(1-2m)/s. The last is the sole additional restriction for v>1/2 and gives v<sqrt(3/4+sqrt(3)/2). Reflection produces precisely the second orientation. The stated local return derivatives are products of signed angle cosines, with modulus less than one on open branch neighborhoods. Replay by the affine candidate and strict branch comparisons in RESULT.md §§1–4. The supplied verifier was inspected, not run; its twelve rational test heights neither establish exhaustion nor prove the equality cases.

originality.rationale: The principal claim is covered by distinct published catalogue statements as of this review. Period three was already credited. The November 8 full-line nonvertex period-four theorem is strictly broader in the height parameter and includes the entire claimed acute census, not merely an example or its height threshold. November 2 explicitly gives the same acute coexistence window. These are later catalogue dates than the frozen record's displayed date, so this is a finding of demonstrable equivalent coverage, not a claim that the frozen authors used those records, that those records were public before the frozen work, or that either has historical priority. The original claimed census and coexistence do not supply a distinct scientific conclusion relative to this evidence.
residual_risks: Catalogue date labels and the available mirror do not resolve historical priority or derivation; coverage is statement-level.
The review is not an exhaustive bibliography of geometric projection dynamics; the located exact matches, not keyword misses, drive the conclusion.

value.rationale: A full-line primitive-period census for a natural discontinuous piecewise contraction is a worthwhile mathematical target. Excluding exterior and repeated-leg cycles and isolating the fixed-tie cutoff makes the sharp coexistence statement stronger than a numerical bifurcation plot. This assessment of the scientific question does not confer originality on an exact classification already represented in the catalogue.
